audits.setting: Orthopaedics department, MVJ Medical College and Research Hospital, tertiary care hospital, Bangalore

audits.title: Improving Discharge Summary Follow-Up Documentation in a Major Trauma Center: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Royal College of Physicians Health Informatics Unit 2019 discharge summary content standards
audits.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Salford Royal NHS Foundation Trust (major trauma centre)

cycle1.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 15.6% (5/32); new medication indication documented 9.4% (3/32); patient advice fully detailed 21.2% (7/33); inpatient management fully detailed 30.3% (10/33).

audits.intervention: Educational poster with a checklist of RCP components, interactive teaching sessions, a discharge summary self-assessment checklist, reminders with one-to-one feedback for junior doctors and a team campaign (August to September 2025).

cycle2.result: Follow-up plan fully detailed 90.0% (18/20) (p < 0.0001); new medication indication 50.0% (9/18) (p = 0.004); patient advice fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.0002); inpatient management fully detailed 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.001).

audits.other_findings: Any safety-net advice fell from 96.9% (32/33) to 76.2% (16/21) (p = 0.02), though when present it was more often excellent. Seven-day readmission was 6.1% vs 4.8%, with no change.
audits.citation: Ahmed H, Mazhar F, Yousaf Z, Akram U, Mazhar S, Rizwan M. Improving Discharge Summary Follow-Up Documentation in a Major Trauma Center: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project. Cureus. 2025;17(12):e99842. doi:10.7759/cureus.99842. PMID: 41573452.

audits.standard: Health Information and Quality Authority (HIQA) seven core data categories for discharge summaries
audits.setting: Internal Medicine Department, Atbara Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Gender documented 46.8%; date of birth 0%; professional role 40.3%.

audits.intervention: Standardised discharge card co-developed with staff, with training.

cycle2.result: Gender 100%; date of birth 5.0% (P = 0.110); professional role 50.0% (P = 0.343).

audits.other_findings: Allergy and contact documentation improved; name, age, primary diagnosis and clinical summary stayed high.

audits.title: Audit and Re-Audit of Discharge Summaries Completeness: A Strategy to Improve Patient Care Quality.
audits.standard: Standardised discharge summary checklist
audits.setting: Department of Surgery and allied specialties, Chaudhary Muhammad Akram Teaching and Research Hospital, Lahore

cycle1.result: Hospital ID 104 (98.9%); full name 92 (87.6%); contact 81 (77.1%); pending investigations 73 (69.5%); biopsy information 66 (62.6%).

cycle2.result: Pending investigations 84 (88.4%); biopsy information 80 (84.2%); red flag symptoms 84 (88.4%); contact 91 (95.8%); follow-up 89 (93.7%).

audits.title: A Closed-Loop Audit of Electronic Discharge Summary Completeness and Safety Netting at Queen Alia Military Hospital in Jordan.
audits.standard: 12-parameter discharge summary checklist including safety-netting items (red-flag symptoms, when to seek help, pending histopathology)
audits.setting: Surgical department, Queen Alia Military Hospital (electronic discharge summaries)

cycle1.result: Most summaries documented only 5-7 of 12 items; very few reached 8-9 items; none included red-flag symptoms, advice on when to seek help or pending histopathology results.

audits.intervention: Resident educational workshops, standardised electronic templates and dedicated documentation time (February 2026).

cycle2.result: Mean completeness 77.04%, with core clinical reporting over 90% compliance.

audits.other_findings: A safety-netting gap persisted after the intervention; a resident survey (n = 15) identified time pressure and lack of training as barriers.
audits.citation: Hamiedah MM, Khamash AH, Ibrahim Al-Arman A, Haddad OJ. A Closed-Loop Audit of Electronic Discharge Summary Completeness and Safety Netting at Queen Alia Military Hospital in Jordan. Cureus. 2026;18(5):e109079. doi:10.7759/cureus.109079. PMID: 42317911.

audits.title: Implementing discharge summary documentation: a quality improvement initiative in a Nigerian hospital.
audits.standard: Discharge summary completion of at least 50% within 12 weeks
audits.setting: General Surgery and Neurosurgery units, Obafemi Awolowo University Teaching Hospitals Complex, Ife

cycle1.result: Completion 0% (0/56) General Surgery, 33% (7/21) Neurosurgery, overall 9% (7/77).

audits.intervention: Discharge summary training at induction, prestructured templates, visual management tools and unit-based champions, tested in PDSA cycles

cycle2.result: Completion 82% (68/83), reaching 100% in some cycles (χ2 = 85.35, p<0.0001); median completion 93.4% General Surgery and 100% Neurosurgery.

audits.other_findings: Baseline survey identified poor knowledge and no standard template as barriers.
audits.citation: Omon H, Owagbemi OF, Ndegbu C, Adesunkanmi A, Balogun S, Ajekwu T, et al.. Implementing discharge summary documentation: a quality improvement initiative in a Nigerian hospital. BMJ Open Qual. 2026;15(3):e003762. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2025-003762. PMID: 42613104.

audits.title: Improving the quality of discharge summaries: implementing updated Academy of Medical Royal Colleges standards at a district general hospital.
audits.standard: Revised Academy of Medical Royal Colleges (AoMRC) discharge summary standards (2013): 23-indicator GP-prioritised minimum dataset
audits.setting: Epsom and St Helier University Hospitals NHS Trust, district general hospital (all inpatient specialties)

cycle1.result: Median compliance 66.7%; mean compliance 57% with iCM-based system vs 77% with InfoPath-based system.

audits.intervention: Single eDS system (iCM-based system withdrawn), new generic template developed with GPs and doctors, and training at junior doctor changeover (August 2014).

cycle2.result: Median compliance 66.7% increased to 77.8%.

audits.other_findings: Average compliance with the full 39-indicator AoMRC standards was 59.5%; completion within 24 hours was not affected and complaints fell.
audits.citation: May-Miller H, Hayter J, Loewenthal L, Hall L, Hilbert R, Quinn M, et al.. Improving the quality of discharge summaries: implementing updated Academy of Medical Royal Colleges standards at a district general hospital. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u207268.w2918. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u207268.w2918. PMID: 26734325.

audits.title: Assessing the impact of a quality improvement program on the quality and timeliness of discharge documents: A before and after study.
audits.standard: National quality of discharge documents (QDD) score; discharge documents given to patient at discharge
audits.setting: University hospital with approximately 40 clinical units using an electronic medical record

cycle1.result: 63% of discharge documents given to patients at discharge; mean QDD score 41 (95%CI [36-46]).

audits.intervention: Quality improvement programme: revision of the EMR, educational programme, audit with scoring and feedback with ranking of clinical units (October 2016 to November 2018).

cycle2.result: 95% of discharge documents given to patients; mean QDD score 82/100 (95% CI [80-85]).

audits.other_findings: Intermediate evaluation (2017): 85% given to patients (P < .001) and mean QDD score 74/100; admission and discharge treatment data remained lowest compliance (44%).
audits.citation: Troude P, Nieto I, Brion A, Goudinoux R, Laganier J, Ducasse V, et al.. Assessing the impact of a quality improvement program on the quality and timeliness of discharge documents: A before and after study. Medicine (Baltimore). 2020;99(51):e23776. doi:10.1097/md.0000000000023776. PMID: 33371146.

audits.setting: Sengkang Community Hospital (SingHealth community hospital)

cycle1.result: Discrepancies in secondary diagnosis capture identified in close to 30% of patients in internal audits.

audits.intervention: Plan-Do-Study-Act cycles combined with change management principles.

cycle2.result: Close to 100% secondary diagnoses capture rate.

audits.other_findings: not reported
